key_insight: Phase-coherent light at ω and 2ω can generate tunable spin photocurrents in centrosymmetric crystals, including symmetry-selected channels with zero charge current.
engineering_relevance: Optical polarization and relative phase offer control parameters for spin-current devices rather than a demonstrated improvement in AI or solar-cell efficiency.
method: Use an inversion-even third-order dc response driven by coherent two-color light.
Analyze magnetic and collinear antiferromagnetic spin point-group symmetries to identify pure-spin channels.
Calculate responses in inversion-stacked bilayer 2H-MoS₂ and a centrosymmetric collinear altermagnet.
evidence_signal: Calculations predict resonantly enhanced, phase-tunable spin photocurrents in systems with strong and weak spin-orbit coupling; the abstract reports no experimental validation.
watch_item: Implementation requires stable relative optical phase and suitable polarization; practical device performance is not established.
paper_title: Two-Color Coherent Control of the Spin Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Crystals
